'''Mara Dierssen Sotos''' (born 21 August 1961) is a Spanish [[neurobiology|neurobiologist]]. She leads the Cellular and Systems Neurobiology group at the [[Centre for Genomic Regulation]] (CRG) in [[Barcelona]] and is regarded as one of the leading international researchers on the neurobiology of [[Down syndrome]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mara Dierssen |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/events/nobel-prize-dialogue/madrid-2024/panelists/mara-dierssen/ |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mara Dierssen, neurobióloga |trans-title=Mara Dierssen, neurobiologist |url=https://mujeresconciencia.com/2016/08/21/mara-dierssen-neurobiologa/ |website=Mujeres con ciencia |language=es |date=21 August 2016 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

Her laboratory identified alterations of [[neuroplasticity|brain plasticity]] in animal models of Down syndrome and took a candidate compound from preclinical work through to a clinical trial, producing the first treatment shown to improve some cognitive functions in people with the condition.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jordana |first=R. |title=Té verde y estimulación cognitiva en síndrome de Down |trans-title=Green tea and cognitive stimulation in Down syndrome |url=https://www.down21.org/noticias/2944-lancet-neurology-te-verde-y-estimulacion-cognitiva-para-la-mejora-de-las-capacidades-en-sindrome-de-down.html |website=Down21 |language=es |date=7 June 2016 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> She has presided over the Spanish Society of Neuroscience, the International Behavioral and Neural Genetics Society and the Trisomy 21 Research Society, and led the organisation of the 2026 [[Federation of European Neuroscience Societies]] (FENS) Forum in Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mara Dierssen: "Barcelona has very solid strengths that will allow it to establish itself as a European leader in brain research" |url=https://www.barcelona.cat/infobarcelona/en/mara-dierssen-barcelona-has-very-solid-strengths-that-will-allow-it-to-establish-itself-as-a-european-leader-in-brain-research_39666.html |website=Info Barcelona |language=en |date=7 July 2026 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Dierssen was born in [[Santander, Spain|Santander]], in the region of [[Cantabria]], the daughter of a painter and a neurosurgeon.<ref>{{cite web |last=Martínez-Campos |first=Maruxa |title="Tenemos mucho que aprender de las personas con discapacidad" |trans-title="We have a lot to learn from people with disabilities" |url=https://www.agenciasinc.es/Entrevistas/Tenemos-mucho-que-aprender-de-las-personas-con-discapacidad |website=Agencia SINC |language=es |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> She graduated in medicine from the [[University of Cantabria]] in 1985 and completed a doctorate in neurobiology at the same university in 1989, with a thesis in [[neuropharmacology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Alumni Mara Dierssen Sotos |trans-title=Alumni Mara Dierssen Sotos |url=https://web.unican.es/Alumni/nuestros-alumni/mara-dierssen-sotos |website=Universidad de Cantabria |language=es |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==

After a research fellowship at the [[Free University of Berlin]] between 1989 and 1990, Dierssen carried out postdoctoral work at the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]] from 1990 to 1993. She then returned to Cantabria as an assistant professor from 1993 to 1997, and from 1997 to 2001 held a research position at the Medical and Molecular Genetics Centre of the Institut de Recerca Oncològica in Barcelona. She has led her own group at the Centre for Genomic Regulation since 2001.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dierssen Lab |url=https://www.crg.eu/en/mara_dierssen |website=Centre for Genomic Regulation |language=en |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In parallel she taught psychobiology at [[Ramon Llull University]] and collaborated in doctoral programmes at the Autonomous University of Barcelona and [[Pompeu Fabra University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Entrevista a Mara Dierssen |trans-title=Interview with Mara Dierssen |url=https://www.down21.org/revista-virtual/541-revista-virtual-2006/revista-virtual-noviembre-2006/entrevista-noviembre-2006/1897-entrevista-a-mara-dierssen.html |website=Down21 |language=es |date=November 2006 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==

Dierssen's laboratory studies the neurobiology of learning and memory and how they are disrupted in brain disorders, with a particular focus on Down syndrome and the [[DYRK1A]] gene, which is present in three copies in [[trisomy 21]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mara Dierssen: «El cerebro ideal es aquel capaz de adaptarse a lo que va sucediendo» |trans-title=Mara Dierssen: "The ideal brain is one capable of adapting to what happens" |url=https://metode.es/noticias/entrevistas/mara-dierssen-sotos.html |website=Mètode |language=es |date=14 December 2017 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In 2016 she and [[María Victoria Sánchez-Vives]] jointly led a study in the ''[[Journal of Neuroscience]]'' showing that overexpression of ''Dyrk1A'' reduces excitability and impairs gamma oscillations in the [[prefrontal cortex]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ruiz-Mejias |first=Marcel |title=Overexpression of Dyrk1A, a Down Syndrome Candidate, Decreases Excitability and Impairs Gamma Oscillations in the Prefrontal Cortex |url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27030752/ |website=PubMed |language=en |date=30 March 2016 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

=== Green tea extract trials ===

Because [[epigallocatechin gallate]] (EGCG), a compound found in [[green tea]], inhibits the DYRK1A protein, Dierssen's group tested it first in mouse models and then in people.<ref>{{cite web |title="Podremos mejorar sustancialmente la capacidad cognitiva en el síndrome de Down" |trans-title="We will be able to substantially improve cognitive capacity in Down syndrome" |url=https://www.sindromedown.org/podremos-mejorar-sustancialmente-la-capacidad-cognitiva-en-el-sindrome-de-down/ |website=Down España |language=es |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> Together with the pharmacologist Rafael de la Torre of the Hospital del Mar Medical Research Institute, she was senior author of the TESDAD trial, a double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study published in ''[[The Lancet Neurology]]'' in 2016. Conducted between June 2012 and June 2014 in 84 participants aged 16 to 34, it found that twelve months of EGCG combined with cognitive training was more effective than cognitive training alone at improving visual recognition memory, inhibitory control and adaptive behaviour.<ref>{{cite web |last=de la Torre |first=Rafael |title=Safety and efficacy of cognitive training plus epigallocatechin-3-gallate in young adults with Down's syndrome (TESDAD): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial |url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27302362/ |website=PubMed |language=en |date=July 2016 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> A paediatric trial in children aged 6 to 12 with Down syndrome and [[fragile X syndrome]] began recruiting in 2018 across five centres in Spain and France, supported by Dierssen's preclinical work.<ref>{{cite web |title=Un compuesto del té verde para mejorar la función cognitiva en el síndrome de Down |trans-title=A green tea compound to improve cognitive function in Down syndrome |url=https://www.agenciasinc.es/Noticias/Un-compuesto-del-te-verde-para-mejorar-la-funcion-cognitiva-en-el-sindrome-de-Down |website=Agencia SINC |language=es |date=21 March 2018 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In a 2020 study in ''[[Scientific Reports]]'' she reported that EGCG combined with environmental enrichment restored more than 70% of the deregulated protein networks in a mouse model, pointing to an [[epigenetics|epigenetic]] mechanism.<ref>{{cite web |title=Potential Down's syndrome treatment may improve cognition through epigenetic activity in brain |url=https://www.crg.eu/en/news/potential-downs-syndrome-treatment-may-improve-cognition-through-epigenetic-activity-brain |website=Centre for Genomic Regulation |language=en |date=29 September 2020 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

=== Retrotransposons and lamivudine ===

In 2024, working with the IrsiCaixa institute, her group showed for the first time that [[retrotransposon]]s are abnormally expressed in Down syndrome and that the antiretroviral drug [[lamivudine]] normalises the expression of several affected genes in a mouse model.<ref>{{cite web |title=Down syndrome linked to changes in mobile DNA fragments |url=https://www.crg.eu/en/news/down-syndrome-linked-changes-mobile-dna-fragments |website=Centre for Genomic Regulation |language=en |date=25 July 2024 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Relacionan el síndrome de Down con fragmentos móviles de ADN y la ayuda de la lamivudina |trans-title=Down syndrome linked to mobile DNA fragments and the help of lamivudine |url=https://www.agenciasinc.es/Noticias/Relacionan-el-sindrome-de-Down-con-fragmentos-moviles-de-ADN-y-la-ayuda-de-la-lamivudina |website=Agencia SINC |language=es |date=26 July 2024 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Scientific societies ==

Dierssen was president of the Spanish Society of Neuroscience from 2013 to 2015 and has also presided over the International Behavioral and Neural Genetics Society.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mara Dierssen |url=https://www.cccb.org/en/w/participants/mara-dierssen |website=Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona |language=en |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> She was a founding member of the Trisomy 21 Research Society, created in 2014, and later served as its president. She has been a member of the executive committee of the Federation of European Neuroscience Societies, chaired the host society committee of the 2012 FENS Forum in Barcelona and was co-chair of the committee for the 2026 edition, held in the same city.<ref>{{cite web |title=FENS Forum 2026: Meet us in Barcelona |url=https://www.fens.org/news-activities/news/fens-forum-2026-meet-us-in-barcelona |website=Federation of European Neuroscience Societies |language=en |date=6 December 2024 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In 2022 she was elected a numerary member of the Royal Academy of Medicine of Catalonia,<ref>{{cite web |title=Elecció de quatre nous Acadèmics Numeraris |trans-title=Election of four new numerary academicians |url=https://ramc.cat/6659-2/ |website=Reial Acadèmia de Medicina de Catalunya |language=ca |date=10 May 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> and she also presides over the Spanish Brain Council.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mara Dierssen: "Invertir en neurociencia es invertir en calidad de vida" |trans-title=Mara Dierssen: "Investing in neuroscience is investing in quality of life" |url=https://www.sindromedown.org/mara-dierssen-invertir-en-neurociencia-es-invertir-en-calidad-de-vida/ |website=Down España |language=es |date=16 April 2026 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* Jaime Blanco Prize, Down Syndrome Foundation of Madrid (twice)
* Ramón Trias Fargas Prize
* National Prize for Thought and Scientific Culture, [[Generalitat de Catalunya]] (2008)
* Sisley-Lejeune Award
* Selección Española de la Ciencia (2016)<ref>{{cite web |title=Selección Española de la Ciencia 2016: Mara Dierssen |trans-title=Spanish Science Team 2016: Mara Dierssen |url=https://www.quo.es/ciencia/a60748/seleccion-espanola-de-la-ciencia-2016-mara-dierssen/ |website=Quo |language=es |date=23 September 2016 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>
* Silver medal and honorary membership of the Official College of Physicians of Cantabria<ref>{{cite web |title=El presidente del Colegio de Médicos de Cantabria entrega a Mara Dierssen la medalla de plata de la institución |trans-title=The president of the College of Physicians of Cantabria presents Mara Dierssen with the institution's silver medal |url=https://www.comcantabria.es/noticias/el-presidente-del-colegio-de-medicos-de-cantabria-entrega-a-mara-dierssen-la-medalla-de-plata-de-la-institucion/ |website=Colegio Oficial de Médicos de Cantabria |language=es |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

She is a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] and of the European Dana Alliance for the Brain, and a distinguished alumna of the University of Cantabria.
